features.name: Basic rename of a primary or remote dentry
features.description: Moves srcdir/srcname to destdir/destname (both paths are dir ino + one name); leader is the destdn auth; reply trace is dest dir + dest dentry + renamed inode.
features.notes: Only depth-1 paths are accepted (EINVAL otherwise).

features.name: Overwrite existing target
features.description: File over file or empty dir over dir; target nlink--, ctime/change_attr bumped, stray_prior_path recorded, STATE_ORPHAN at nlink 0; primary target re-homed into the leader's stray dir.
features.notes: mgr/volumes relies on atomic replace for .meta files.

features.name: Same-inode and same-dentry no-op
features.description: destdn == srcdn returns 0; two hard links to the same inode (source dir not stray) returns 0 without changes.
features.notes: In charmap (case-insensitive) dirs names folding to one dentry hit the first case.

features.name: Directory loop prevention
features.description: EINVAL when srci is a directory and a projected ancestor of destdir.
features.notes: Correctness depends on ancestor snaplock rdlocks preventing concurrent ancestor renames.

features.name: Type and emptiness checks
features.description: EISDIR (dir target, file source), ENOTDIR (file target, dir source), ENOTEMPTY (unlocked fast check then locked check with filelock rdlock).
features.notes: Unlocked check treats a dir with cached filelock (pending async dirops) as possibly empty.

features.name: Input validation
features.description: EBUSY for . or .. last component; ENAMETOOLONG for alternate_name > mds_alternate_name_max; EINVAL for depth != 1; EROFS for .snap paths and system (non-root) parents; ENOENT for unlinked destination parent or missing source.
features.notes: Source parent being unlinked is not rejected.

features.name: Cross-subvolume EXDEV
features.description: EXDEV when src and dest parents are in different snaprealms whose subvolume_ino differ (inside vs outside, or two different subvolumes).
features.notes: Quota realm boundaries are not enforced by the MDS; clients return EXDEV for cross-quota-realm renames.

features.name: alternate_name (fscrypt) on rename
features.description: Null destination dentry takes the request's alternate_name; existing destination with different alternate_name gives EINVAL; alternate_name is replicated to witnesses.
features.notes: Kernel calls fscrypt_prepare_rename before sending.

features.name: Charmap feature gate
features.description: EPERM if the destination dir has a charmap and the session lacks CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP.
features.notes: Only the destination dir is checked.

features.name: Quarantine blocking for old clients
features.description: Requests from clients without CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE wait while either parent is under a quarantined subvolume.

features.name: MDS auth-cap checks
features.description: MAY_WRITE on source dir inode, destination dir inode and the renamed inode, evaluated only before any witness acked; EACCES on denial.
features.notes: POSIX permission and sticky-bit checks are left to clients.

features.name: Directory size limits
features.description: ENOSPC when the destination dirfrag reaches mds_bal_fragment_size_max, when the destination dir reaches mds_dir_max_entries, or when the chosen stray dirfrag is full.
features.notes: Skipped for link merges; stray check skipped for replayed requests.

features.name: Full metadata pool handling
features.description: While the metadata pool has FLAG_FULL and no witness has acked, rename is refused unless the session MDS cap allows 'full' (checked on the destination dir inode). The intended error is ENOSPC, but Server::check_access already replies EACCES, so the client first sees EACCES and then a duplicate ENOSPC reply (found by reading the code).
features.notes: The double reply looks like a C++ bug; clients drop the second reply because its tid is unknown.

features.name: Forwarding to destination dentry auth
features.description: Destination traversal uses WANT_AUTH so the request is forwarded to the auth of the destination dirfrag; source traversal uses DISCOVER and replicates remote metadata.
features.notes: Clients route rename by the destination dentry.

features.name: Two-path lock ordering
features.description: Ancestor snaplock rdlocks for both paths, dir filelock/nestlock wrlocks (remote wrlock to srcdir frag auth), dentry xlocks; ordering by root tree, depth, ino, dentry name; then srci/oldin linklock+snaplock xlocks ordered by path/ino, oldin filelock rdlock, stray locks.
features.notes: sort_and_merge sorts only within one object.

features.name: Stray dentry and deferred purge of overwritten inode
features.description: Overwritten primary inode moves to ~mds<leader>/stray<k>/<ino hex>; StrayManager evaluates it after the reply (purge or later reintegration).
features.notes: Keeps open-but-replaced files readable until caps are released.

features.name: Snapshot copy-on-write of old dentries
features.description: journal_cow_dentry preserves old src/dest dentries (and COW inodes) for snapshots covering them; new linkages get first = newest_seq + 1.

features.name: past_parent_snaps and realm split on cross-realm move
features.description: Moving an inode covered by snapshots out of its realm opens/updates a snaprealm with past_parent_snaps; clients get CEPH_SNAP_OP_SPLIT for srci.
features.notes: The overwritten inode's realm split is not notified to clients.

features.name: Global snaprealm handling for hard-linked inodes
features.description: Inodes with PARENT_GLOBAL realms record the parent dentry's snaps on rename and drop the global flag when the last (remote) link goes away or on link merge.
features.notes: Global realms are only used for hard links outside subvolumes.

features.name: Cross-MDS two-phase commit
features.description: Leader (destdn auth) sends OP_RENAMEPREP to all replicas of srcdn/destdn, srcdn auth (last) and remote srci/oldin auths; peers journal EPeerUpdate PREPARE with a rollback record; leader journals EUpdate(had_peers); OP_FINISH commits; OP_COMMITTED then ECommitted.
features.notes: Internal protocol; not a contract for a Rust MDS that never mixes with C++ ranks.

features.name: Inode authority and cap migration during rename
features.description: When srcdn is primary on another rank, srci is frozen there, exported with caps in the prepare ack, imported by the leader (force-opening client sessions, CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT), and the exporter sends CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT on commit.
features.notes: Directory renames move only the inode; dirfrags keep their old authority as subtree roots.

features.name: Bystander notify and client session flush
features.description: srcdn auth sends OP_RENAMENOTIFY to srcdn replicas and CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG to clients holding caps on srci, waiting for all acks before the final prepare.
features.notes: A client that never answers FLUSHMSG stalls the rename.

features.name: Ambiguous auth on the renamed inode
features.description: STATE_AMBIGUOUSAUTH on srci at all participants while its authority changes; other requests wait for WAIT_SINGLEAUTH.

features.name: Peer rollback
features.description: Rollback from rename_rollback: relink srcdn, restore destdn/target nlink and srnodes, repair source dirfrag stats, journal EPeerUpdate ROLLBACK.
features.notes: ctime/mtime restoration never fires because rollback.ctime/old_ctime are never set.

features.name: Recovery of in-flight renames via resolve
features.description: uncommitted_leaders / uncommitted_peers, MMDSResolve peer_requests (with cap exports), MMDSResolveAck commit/abort, ambiguous peer updates when srcdn auth fails, pending_leaders delay, finish_committed_leaders.
features.notes: Clients resend unsafe requests after failover; completed-request table makes them idempotent.

features.name: Leader journaling
features.description: EUpdate type rename with client req, metablob, optional client_map/cmapv, reqid/had_peers; ECommitted after all peers committed.
features.notes: On-disk format is free for the Rust MDS.

features.name: Peer journaling
features.description: EPeerUpdate peer_rename_prep (OP_PREPARE with commit metablob + rollback), peer_rename_commit (OP_COMMIT), peer_rename_rollback (OP_ROLLBACK); skipped entirely when the peer is auth for nothing.

features.name: Forced journaling for subtree owners
features.description: A rank owning subtrees nested under a renamed dir (or under the replaced target dir) journals the new location even if it is not auth for the dentries (renamed_dirino, renamed_dir_frags).

features.name: Subtree map maintenance for directory renames
features.description: project_subtree_rename queues in-flight renames for ESubtreeMap; adjust_subtree_after_rename moves bounds and creates subtrees when parent authorities differ.

features.name: need_flush before witnesses
features.description: If witnesses exist and any dentry on the traces is projected, wait for the whole log to be safe before sending prepares.
features.notes: Because replicas cannot see projected linkages.

features.name: Early (unsafe) reply rules
features.description: Unsafe reply only without journaled peers; dentry xlocks are not marked done for rename; ISNAP/IPOLICY rdlocks kept until safe.
features.notes: Client must treat unsafe reply as success and wait for safe for durability.

features.name: Reply trace and dentry lease
features.description: Trace = destination dir inode, its dirstat, destination name, dentry lease (if lockable), renamed inode stat; snapbl of srci realm.
features.notes: Clients accept traceless replies and then move the dentry themselves.

features.name: Client cap and lease revocation
features.description: Dentry xlocks revoke dentry leases (MClientLease REVOKE); srci/oldin linklock xlocks revoke Ls/Lx; dir filelock wrlocks force Fs revocation; clients pre-drop via embedded releases.
features.notes: libcephfs also breaks NFS delegations on source and target.

features.name: Attribute updates from client stamp
features.description: ctime/rctime/change_attr on renamed and replaced inodes; parent dir fragstat mtime/change_attr and nfiles/nsubdirs; values come from the client request stamp when present.
features.notes: Stray reintegration/migration is silent (no changes).

features.name: rstat/dirstat propagation
features.description: predirty_journal_parents adjusts fragstat and rstat on source and destination parents, stray dir, and remote-link primary parents. The source-side call passes PREDIRTY_SHALLOW, but the flag is only logged, so propagation is not actually limited (MDCache.cc:2231).
features.notes: Clients read rstats via ceph.dir.r* vxattrs and quota enforcement.

features.name: Backtrace update
features.description: Renamed inode and stray-bound target get update_backtrace and STATE_DIRTYPARENT; parent/layout xattrs rewritten on the first object at segment expiry.
features.notes: Used by data-scan/scrub tools; internal format.

features.name: Stray reintegration
features.description: MDS-originated rename of a stray primary onto one of its remote dentries (link merge), silent.
features.notes: Needed to keep hard links working after the primary link was removed.

features.name: Stray migration
features.description: MDS-originated stray->stray rename to another rank (e.g. to rank 0 while stopping), implemented as a rename with inode export.

features.name: Completed-request idempotency
features.description: Rename reqids are journaled (add_client_req); resent/replayed requests found in the session completed table are answered 0 without re-execution.

features.name: Notify non-witness replicas
features.description: send_dentry_link sends MDentryLink to replicas of destdn that were not witnesses.

features.name: Balancer hooks
features.description: META_POP_IWR hits on source dir (and srci), maybe_fragment on destination dir, popularity moved for dir renames.

features.name: Embedded cap/dentry releases
features.description: Releases carried in the rename request (Fs/Xx on both dentries unless Fx, Ls/Lx on source, unlink-style drop on target) are applied before dispatch, so the MDS can take its locks without waiting for revokes. They are skipped for replayed requests.
features.notes: A latency optimisation; an MDS that ignored releases would still be correct, only slower.

features.name: Degraded-cluster wait for snaplock xlock
features.description: Rename xlocks srci (and oldin) snaplock. While the cluster is degraded, the leader waits for the whole cluster to recover if that inode is not auth, or is replicated on a rank below active.
features.notes: Externally visible as renames stalling during any rank's recovery.

features.name: Test hooks
features.description: mds_kill_rename_at (1,3,4,5,6,7) kill points and mds_inject_rename_corrupt_dentry_first.
features.notes: QA only.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: all dispatch, retries and journal completions run under the big lock
serialization_points.notes: Rename never blocks a thread but holds mds_lock for all its CPU work.

serialization_points.name: Dentry xlocks (srcdn, destdn, straydn)
serialization_points.why_serialized: only one mutation of a name at a time; revoke client dentry leases
serialization_points.notes: Held until the safe reply (not marked done on early reply).

serialization_points.name: Parent dir filelock/nestlock wrlocks
serialization_points.shared_state: dirfrag fnode fragstat/rstat, dir inode dirstat
serialization_points.why_serialized: consistent dir size/mtime/rstat; excludes readers needing SYNC (readdir, Fs caps)
serialization_points.notes: Shared among mutators; remote wrlock when srcdir frag is on another rank.

serialization_points.name: Ancestor snaplock rdlocks vs dir rename snaplock xlock
serialization_points.shared_state: ancestry and snaprealm membership of every path component
serialization_points.why_serialized: prevent loops and realm changes while paths are used
serialization_points.notes: Renaming dir D waits for all in-flight ops traversing D and blocks new ones until safe reply; file renames pay the same rdlocks.

serialization_points.name: srci linklock/snaplock xlock
serialization_points.why_serialized: ctime update and realm stability
serialization_points.notes: Remote xlock (OP_XLOCK) if srci is not local.

serialization_points.name: oldin linklock/snaplock xlock + filelock rdlock
serialization_points.why_serialized: nlink-- and empty-dir verification must be stable

serialization_points.name: versionlock wrlock (leader) / xlock (peer)
serialization_points.why_serialized: pipeline journal updates on leader; make peer rollback safe
serialization_points.notes: Peer side is exclusive until commit/rollback.

serialization_points.name: Upward rstat propagation
serialization_points.shared_state: ancestor nestlock/versionlock and projected inodes up to root
serialization_points.why_serialized: recursive stats
serialization_points.notes: Best effort: stops and marks scatterlock dirty if a parent nestlock cannot be wrlocked.

serialization_points.name: Freeze of srci on srcdn auth
serialization_points.why_serialized: inode authority migration must not race with other updates
serialization_points.notes: Also frozen auth pin during the lock phase (Server.cc:3373).

serialization_points.name: Ambiguous auth on srci
serialization_points.why_serialized: no forwarding/auth pins while authority is in flux
serialization_points.notes: Cluster-wide for the duration of the 2PC.

serialization_points.name: Client session flush
serialization_points.shared_state: client message ordering for caps on srci
serialization_points.why_serialized: clients must have processed prior cap messages before cap export
serialization_points.notes: Round trip to every client with caps on srci.

serialization_points.name: Bystander rename notify
serialization_points.shared_state: lock messages from srcdn auth to replicas
serialization_points.why_serialized: causal ordering across ranks

serialization_points.name: Witness fan-out to all replicas
serialization_points.why_serialized: replicas must stay connected; rejoin relies on it
serialization_points.notes: Code comment says probably unnecessary for file renames.

serialization_points.name: need_flush wait
serialization_points.shared_state: journal safety of earlier projected dentries
serialization_points.why_serialized: replicas cannot see projected linkages
serialization_points.notes: Waits for the whole rank log to be safe.

serialization_points.name: Per-rank journal ordering of prepare/update/commit
serialization_points.why_serialized: durability order of 2PC phases
serialization_points.notes: Leader journal waits for every peer prepare; ECommitted after all OP_COMMITTED.

serialization_points.name: Uncommitted leader/peer bookkeeping and segment expiry
serialization_points.why_serialized: cannot trim journal before 2PC completes

serialization_points.name: Subtree map and projected_subtree_renames
serialization_points.why_serialized: subtree bounds change on dir renames

serialization_points.name: Stray directory selection and capacity
serialization_points.why_serialized: overwritten primaries need a stray dentry on the leader
serialization_points.notes: ENOSPC possible when the stray frag is full.

serialization_points.name: quiescelock wrlock
serialization_points.shared_state: quiesce barrier of the first cap-bearing inode per lock batch
serialization_points.why_serialized: quiesce must block mutations
serialization_points.notes: Only one inode per acquire_locks call gets it. Remote OP_XLOCK/OP_WRLOCK requests on peers skip it (Server.cc:3233, skip_quiesce=true).

serialization_points.name: Snaplock xlock waits for cluster recovery
serialization_points.shared_state: ordering of replayed requests vs. new snap/policy changes
serialization_points.why_serialized: replayed requests and mksnap/setlayout must be processed in order while ranks recover
serialization_points.notes: Every rename xlocks srci->snaplock, so renames of non-auth inodes, or of inodes replicated on recovering ranks, stall until all ranks are active.

serialization_points.name: Sequential remote lock acquisition
serialization_points.shared_state: locks on objects owned by other ranks
serialization_points.why_serialized: acquire_locks returns after each remote lock request and restarts on the ack
serialization_points.notes: Remote auth pins go out in parallel, one OP_AUTHPIN per rank (Locker.cc:523-557). Remote xlocks/wrlocks cost one round trip each.

external_contract.detail: CEPH_MDS_OP_RENAME 0x01204, path1 = dest dir ino + name, path2 = src dir ino + name, alternate_name, releases (Fs|Xx unless Fx on both dentries, Ls|Lx on source inode, unlink-drop on target), stamp = client coarse real time.
renameat2 flags -> EINVAL, different snap -> EXDEV, cross quota realm -> EXDEV, snapdir -> RENAMESNAP; these never reach the MDS.

is_dentry trace with dir inode == request parent (destination dir) and dentry name == destination; is_target = renamed inode; kernel BUG_ONs on mismatch; d_move done on trace, or by ceph_rename on traceless reply.
Unsafe reply carries result and trace; safe reply after unsafe is not parsed; request tracked as unsafe dirop on the old dir.

EBUSY, ENAMETOOLONG, EINVAL, EROFS, ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EISDIR, ENOTEMPTY, EXDEV, ENOSPC, EACCES (also returned on a full metadata pool to sessions without the 'full' cap), EPERM, ESTALE, EIO. EAGAIN cannot occur for rename (no non-blocking auth pins).
MClientLease CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE on src/dest names; client answers CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE_ACK.
CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG from srcdn auth; client flushes cap releases and answers FLUSHMSG_ACK; rename waits for it.
CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT from new auth (peer = old auth cap id/seq/mseq, CEPH_CAP_FLAG_AUTH) and CEPH_CAP_OP_EXPORT from old auth, in either order.
CEPH_SNAP_OP_SPLIT with split_inos/split_realms when a snaprealm is opened on the renamed inode (or merged back on rollback).
MClientRequestForward to the destination dentry auth.
ctime of renamed/replaced inode and parent dir mtime/ctime come from the request stamp.

Client::_rename: path walks, ENOKEY for locked fscrypt dirs, EXDEV across quota roots when client_quota, may_delete checks, releases Fs (unless Fx) on dentries, Ls on source, Ls|Lx on target; breaks delegations.
insert_trace moves the old Dentry to the new name; traceless reply unlinks old dentry and clears dir complete.
Uses ceph_ll_rename (assumed; Ganesha source not in tree); depends on delegation breaks and change_attr bumps on parents and inodes.
Goes through kernel VFS then Client::ll_rename; same contract as libcephfs.
Renames .meta.tmp over .meta inside a subvolume; requires atomic overwrite.
Renames subvolume incarnations into the subvolume .trash and entities into /volumes/_deleting; requires same-subvolume renames and moving subvolume roots between non-subvolume parents to succeed.
mgr/volumes sets ceph.dir.subvolume=1; MDS refuses renames whose parents are in different subvolumes.
Asynchronous dirfrag omap updates in source/destination/stray dirfrag objects and backtrace parent/layout xattrs on first objects; journal objects for EUpdate/EPeerUpdate/ECommitted.
cephfs-data-scan/cephfs-journal-tool read backtraces and EUpdate/EPeerUpdate encodings (internal format, replaceable).
mds_alternate_name_max, mds_bal_fragment_size_max, mds_dir_max_entries, mds_early_reply, mds_kill_rename_at; mds_server.req_rename_latency, mds_cache.strays_reintegrated/strays_migrated.

rust_implications.implication: In C++ inode authority follows the primary dentry, so a cross-rank rename migrates the inode and all client caps (freeze, ambiguous auth, FLUSHMSG, cap export/import). If Rust shards own inodes independently of dentry location, only the dentry-level change needs cross-shard 2PC and cap migration is avoided; clients still must see consistent cap ownership (one auth MDS per inode).

C++ already returns EXDEV for renames whose parents are in different subvolumes (or one inside, one outside). With subvolumes as autonomous shards, rename never needs a cross-subvolume transaction; only intra-subvolume cross-dirfrag/cross-shard renames need 2PC. Keep the exact rule (compare parents' realms, allow moving a subvolume root between non-subvolume parents) because mgr/volumes depends on it.

rust_implications.topic: Loop prevention without global path locks
rust_implications.implication: C++ prevents loops by rdlocking snaplocks of all ancestors of both parents for every rename and xlocking the renamed dir's snaplock. A Rust design can restrict the expensive ancestry protection to directory renames (file renames cannot create loops) e.g. with a per-subvolume directory-rename lock or ordered ancestor locks up to the common ancestor.

Renaming dir D in C++ blocks all in-flight and new operations under D until the safe reply (snaplock xlock vs traversal rdlocks). An intent-lock (IX/X) hierarchy can give the same correctness with a narrower window (e.g. release after the namespace change is durable in the shard journal).

C++ allows concurrent renames/creates/unlinks of distinct names in one dir (shared wrlocks on scatter locks + per-dentry xlocks) but everything still runs under mds_lock and one journal. Rust can execute them truly in parallel with per-dentry X locks and commutative dir stat deltas.

Must return a trace whose dir inode is the destination dir and dentry is the destination name with the renamed inode as target (kclient BUG_ONs otherwise), or a traceless reply. Must honour unsafe/safe reply semantics and completed-request idempotency by tid across failover.

Before the change becomes visible: revoke dentry leases on both names, revoke Ls/Lx on renamed and replaced inodes, and invalidate Fs-based dir caching on both parents (or otherwise guarantee clients drop dir completeness); process embedded releases first.

Replaced inodes with open handles/caps must survive until caps are released (C++ uses a stray dentry and StrayManager purge). Rust needs an equivalent orphan list per shard and deferred data purge; nlink and ctime of the replaced inode change as POSIX requires.

A renamed inode leaving a snapshotted realm must keep visibility in old snapshots (past_parent_snaps) and old names must remain in snapshots (dentry COW). Clients must receive realm SPLIT updates so their snap contexts for writeback are right. If Rust snapshots are per-subvolume only, intra-subvolume renames still cross nested realms.
Use the client-provided request stamp for ctime/mtime; bump change_attr on the renamed inode, replaced inode and both parent dirs (Ganesha change_info).

C++ uses leader journal + peer prepare journals with rollback blobs, OP_FINISH/OP_COMMITTED/ECommitted and a resolve phase; peers xlock versionlocks to make rollback safe. Rust can use a cleaner 2PC with explicit intents per shard journal; note the C++ rollback does not restore ctime/mtime (fields never populated), so exact rollback of timestamps is not an existing contract.

C++ must contact every rank that replicates srcdn/destdn because of replicated cache coherence. A Rust design without cross-rank metadata replication (or with invalidation-based replicas) avoids this fan-out entirely.

C++ distinguishes primary vs remote dentries and needs stray reintegration/migration renames to keep hard links working after the primary is unlinked. With a free on-disk format, Rust can store inodes by ino and treat all links equally, eliminating linkmerge/reintegration as a rename variant, while preserving nlink semantics and the 'same inode -> no-op' rule.

Match the C++ error ordering where clients may observe it (EBUSY for dot names before path checks, ENOTEMPTY/EISDIR/ENOTDIR before access checks, EXDEV last), and keep ENOSPC conditions (fragment size, dir max entries) as admin-visible limits if equivalent options exist.
Renames must be blockable by subvolume quiesce (C++ via quiescelock wrlock on the first cap-bearing inode per lock batch); a Rust subvolume quiesce should block rename at the shard level.

C++ makes a leader wait for full cluster recovery before xlocking a snaplock on a non-auth inode, or on one replicated on a rank below active (Locker.cc:275-307). Every rename xlocks srci->snaplock, so renames stall during any rank's recovery. A design whose recovery is scoped to one shard can keep renames in unaffected shards available. Clients only need to tolerate delays, which they already do.

By code reading, C++ answers a rename on a full metadata pool from a session without the 'full' cap with EACCES and then a duplicate ENOSPC reply. Clients drop the duplicate (unknown tid). A Rust MDS should send exactly one reply; ENOSPC is the intended semantics, and kclient/libcephfs handle either code.

open_questions: Possible self-deadlock: renaming a directory onto a directory that is an ancestor of the source parent, while the target's filelock is cached (async dirops), would xlock a snaplock the request already rdlocks from source traversal (Server.cc:9391, Locker.cc:157, Locker.cc:2137). If correct, the snaplock stays in LOCK_SYNC_LOCK and new traversals through the target dir block too. The kernel VFS prevents this case; direct libcephfs callers might not. Not reproduced.
do_rename_rollback computes force_journal_dest with _need_force_journal(in, true) where 'in' is the renamed inode, not the restored target dir (Server.cc:11077-11078); intentional or bug?

rename_rollback.ctime and drec.old_ctime are never filled in handle_peer_rename_prep, so ctime/mtime restoration in rollback is dead code; confirm whether any client-visible behaviour depends on this.

Exact interplay between kclient async dirops (Fx + DIR_CREATE/UNLINK caps and lock caches) and rename on the same directory is only partially traced here; see leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops page.
NFS-Ganesha FSAL_CEPH usage of ceph_ll_rename and its reliance on change_attr/delegation semantics is assumed, not verified against Ganesha source.
When the overwritten target is remote-linked and nlink drops to 0, purge relies on later reference drops calling maybe_eval_stray; timing guarantees are not explicit.

Full metadata pool: dispatch_client_request calls check_access(MAY_FULL), which itself replies EACCES, and then calls respond_to_request(-ENOSPC) again (Server.cc:2829-2834). Found by reading the code: the client sees EACCES plus a duplicate reply. Not tested at runtime.

Target-dir snapshot check: _dir_is_nonempty_unlocked returns early when the target's filelock is cached (async dirops), skipping the own-realm snapshot test. The locked _dir_is_nonempty does not look at snapshots, so an empty target dir that has snapshots may be replaced (rmdir has the same path). Found by reading the code only.

PREDIRTY_SHALLOW (passed for the source parent) is never honoured by predirty_journal_parents (only logged, MDCache.cc:2231). Is any rollback assumption broken because propagation is deeper than the flag's comment implies?

The 'merging remote onto primary link' branches in _rename_prepare (Server.cc:10027-10033) and _rename_apply (10403-10406), and the 'nlink-- on linkmerge' (10074-10075), look unreachable: linkmerge implies a primary source in a stray dir (silent). Dead code or a latent path?
